feature: A captured changing-weather expedition through matched private evolutionary futures
changes: Plan a weather expedition navigation opens a lazy investigation after the main archipelago scene. Four upcoming generations can have different rainfall on a chosen island; other islands retain captured baseline conditions.
Native schedule sliders and gradual/abrupt/steady presets let learners define a changing habitat. A nonempty prediction is captured before generating outcomes.

Changing and steady rainfall futures use the exact existing genetics kernel, identical starting organisms and the same initial private RNG seed. Recorded expedition history and its next future stay unchanged.

Side-by-side cohort cards, a selectable full-precision trait chart, a schematic rainfall/traits island map and generation/species/island/condition controls connect scheduled conditions with recorded offspring cohorts.

Controlled playback visits already computed generations, with pause and manual previous/next controls. Manual view navigation and closing the investigation pause playback; no new simulation runs during playback.
A read-only captured rainfall-plan review and locked prediction distinguish results from later draft, environmental-setting or expedition edits.
Private organism selectors expose actual two-parent inheritance and independent marker copies, with the existing allele-to-founder passport scoped to the chosen private branch.
Selection-off experiments provide an exact null control: paired organisms, inheritance, migration records and RNG remain identical regardless of the rainfall sequence.
Repeating keeps the captured source, schedule and prediction while changing the private random batch. Saved compact recipes explicitly replay and rebuild their outcomes, view and explanation.

Separate Learning Journal findings and JSON exports include captured source checkpoint, schedule, private batch, full-precision series and selected view. Displayed trajectory table means use four decimals.

scientificBoundaries: Rainfall is an illustrative0to1 habitat index, not an empirical weather series, climate projection or complete ecosystem forecast.
Changing rainfall affects relative breeding weights only when selection is on. It never edits living organisms or makes mutation respond to environmental need.

Both private branches restore identical source organisms and share an initial private seed. Changed parent choices and their later descendants are stochastic model outcomes; one pair is not proof of adaptation or a unique causal decomposition.
Dispersal, mutation, reciprocal partner effects and all other settings stay at captured values. Both fictional species reproduce with the existing finite-population engine.
Series row zero is the shared starting cohort and has null future rainfall. Subsequent weather rows are captured conditions used to produce each recorded cohort.
With selection off, all breeding weights equal1 and rainfall has no model effect. Paired cohorts and inheritance are identical; weather settings may differ or match.
Repeated private batches are possible futures conditional on the same captured organisms, not independent founder populations or field samples.
Playback visits recorded cohort snapshots; lines do not represent continuous genetic change within individual organisms.
The map is schematic and adds no local selection, demographic resource dynamics, predator cycles or unmodeled processes.
Neutral marker H remains a one-locus copy-based statistic. Changing trait means alone do not establish real-world coevolution, genome-wide diversity or speciation.
Private IDs and ancestry belong to their selected branch. They cannot replace the recorded expedition’s organism inspector or genealogy.
